title: Per-Representative Performance — What the Numbers Actually Show
content:
###  **The Learning Curve Problem** 

A newly hired canvasser needs weeks, sometimes longer, to become genuinely effective at homeowner conversations. That ramp-up period is unpaid productivity from the company's perspective — real wages, limited results. 

###  **Why Trained Representatives Perform Differently** 

A representative who has already been through structured training and ongoing supervision starts from a different baseline. The learning curve most companies pay for internally has already happened. 

###  **What This Means Per Person** 

On a per-representative basis, this often means more consistent, higher-quality conversations from day one — without the company absorbing the training investment or the risk of an early departure. 

###  **Worth Understanding Before Hiring** 

Before investing in hiring and training a new in-house canvasser, it is worth understanding what a trained representative can typically produce by comparison.
